newsitem.title: USA: Apple shrs up amid Jobs chairman reports.
newsitem.headline: Apple shrs up amid Jobs chairman reports.

text.p: Shares of Apple Computer Inc rose in active trade after persistent published reports and speculation on the Internet that co-founder Steve Jobs will be named its next chairman.

Apple shares were up one at 17-1/2 in late morning, after trading as high as $17.6875, their level in mid-May before a June tumble in which they fell as low as 12-3/4 before the ouster of Gilbert Amelio as chief executive in early July.
The San Francisco Chronicle reported in its Wednesday editions that Apple is planning to introduce Jobs as chairman during next week's Macworld Expo trade show in Boston.

The report follows a flurry of speculation in Internet discussion groups and electronic mail that Jobs would be handed the chairmanship at Apple. Twelve years ago, Jobs was forced to step down as John Sculley consolidated control.
An Apple spokeswoman declined comment on the rumor.
"It's a rumor, that's all it is, and we absolutely do not comment on rumors," said the spokeswoman.

Apple did confirm that Jobs, who has been a strategic adviser at Apple since Amelio decided to acquire Jobs' Next Software late last year, would be speaking at the MacWorld trade show next Wednesday morning, however.

The San Jose Mercury News, which first reported last Saturday that Jobs would soon be made chairman, said Wednesday that several sources close to Apple had said the company was trying to time the appointment to coincide with the MacWorld trade show and Jobs's keynote speech.

Analysts said a return by Jobs to the chairmanship of the company he founded with Steve Wozniak in a Silicon Valley garage would help restore hope among Apple's most loyal customers as the company's market share is dwindling.
Apple insiders have poiinted in recent weeks to Jobs's growing influence even before Amelio's ouster, saying he was taking a key role in many recent decisions at the company.

"If it is true that Jobs is going to take this type of leadership role, I would expect that the rationale would be for him to be a focal point to rally the troops," said Tim Bajarin, president of Creative Strategies Research International.
"I think he's the only one who could do it at this point, given the fact that it was his company at one point and he's still really tied to the Macintosh vision," Bajarin added.
"In the short term, can you at least provide the Macintosh (personal computer) fans a sense of hope."

Sources close to Apple said Jobs's role would be to establish a broad vision for the company, renewing the confidence of employees, customers and investors, but they also consider the appointment of Jobs to be a vote for Apple's continued independence.
"I would be very surprised if Jobs's role is to try to sell the company," one said.
